rule: At least 14 days at a rung before advancing (21 days before the unrestricted top rungs)
summary: Tendon and connective tissue adapt more slowly than muscle (Kjaer 2009; Mersmann 2017), with measurable tendon changes over 8-12+ week interventions (Bohm 2015 MA), so a time floor alongside performance criteria is physiologically sensible; ACL cohort data show time and criteria each reduce reinjury. No evidence tests 14 days per rung specifically; across a 3-4 rung ladder it gives a 6-10 week minimum, which sits near the tendon-adaptation time scale. Heuristic, cheap relative to a back/shoulder setback.

sources.note: Bohm 2015 MA (27 studies): tendon stiffness adapts to loading magnitude over >= 8-12 week interventions; larger effects with >= 12 weeks
Kjaer 2009 review: tendon adaptation to chronic loading takes longer than muscle; collagen synthesis responds to strain
Mersmann 2017 review: muscle and tendon adapt on different time courses; imbalance may raise tendon overload risk
Delaware-Oslo ACL cohort: both time (each month of delay to 9 mo cut reinjury 51%) and passing function criteria lowered reinjury: time AND criteria both matter
